metrics.sourceCitation: EASI fixed criteria, Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)
metrics.howToMeasure: Impervious surface (%) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <10%, Fair 10-25%, Poor >25%.
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in impervious surface. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
metrics.methodContext: Percent of the watershed in woody plus herbaceous wetland (NLCD 2019). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional

curveCaveats: Built from 19 reference sites (exploratory band, below the automated floor of 20): the point value carries wide sampling error.
Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.

In the discrimination check this curve scored pressured stations above reference stations (area under the curve 0.16), so the score may not track condition here. Read it with the other metrics of the function.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)
localComparison.definition: stations of this ecoregion that pass the relaxed pressure screen

metrics.sourceCitation: EASI fixed criteria, Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure
metrics.howToMeasure: Road density (km/sq km) is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good <1 km/km², Fair 1-<3 km/km², Poor ≥3 km/km².
metrics.methodContext: Road length per square kilometer of watershed. DEEP computes it for the delineated watershed. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Road-density proxy for concentrated inflow pressure

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.

metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
metrics.methodContext: Base flow index of the watershed, the percent of streamflow that comes from base flow (USGS base flow index grid). DEEP reads it from EPA StreamCat for the reach. Nothing is measured in the field.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional

curveCaveats: Built from 19 reference sites (exploratory band, below the automated floor of 20): the point value carries wide sampling error.
Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.

referenceSupport.basisStatement: Reference curve fitted to least-disturbed stations selected by a fixed landscape-pressure screen.

localComparison.label: Local best-available comparison (not reference)

criteriaSource.title: Catchment hydrology (land-cover pressure)

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
Schueler 1994, The importance of imperviousness
Allan 2004, Landscapes and riverscapes: the influence of land use on stream ecosystems
Wang et al. 1997, Influences of watershed land use on habitat quality and biotic integrity in Wisconsin streams
King et al. 2011, Stream community thresholds at exceptionally low levels of catchment urbanization

limitations: The worse input governs because hydrologic alteration through one pathway is not offset by low pressure in the other.
Agricultural bands are national screening tiers, not ecological criteria.
A result computed from one input is labeled partial.

Sensitive macroinvertebrate taxa decline well below the 10 percent impervious Good boundary (community thresholds near 0.5 to 2 percent), so a Good rating is not a no-effect finding (King et al. 2011).

citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 11 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 2 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

library.revisionNotes: Methodology 0.12 rebuild: reference stations selected by the fixed pressure screen, pools assembled per metric on the Level III to Level I ladder, and the five landscape pressure metrics scored on the fixed criteria of the Screening tier. No candidate inside this ecoregion passes the screen, so all 16 reference curves are borrowed from a comparable Level II or Level I pool under the comparability check, with the source geography and transfer risk recorded on each. Sixteen curves cover 16 of the 20 STAF functions. The four remaining functions carry a documented gap for insufficient reference support rather than a forced curve. The fast-water habitat curve is marked for verification against field data before it carries weight in a decision.

exclusions.justification: Every candidate metric for this function was withheld. The scored candidates are benthic total taxa richness and native fish taxa richness, and native non-tolerant fish taxa richness was also tested under Pre-registration III. Too few comparable least-disturbed stations carry them in this ecoregion or in its Level II and Level I parents. On comparable national donors the strongest result was native non-tolerant fish taxa richness on distance-matched donors, which reached promising: its class calls agreed with reference in 16 of 19 evaluation regions with no systematic promotion, but its recovered thresholds fell inside the true answer's uncertainty in only 9 of 19, against the 13 required to validate. No modeled expectation passed validation under the extrapolation this ecoregion requires. Ohio EPA's ecoregional biocriteria, the nearest applicable published criterion, were checked on 2026-09-21 and are not usable here on three independent grounds. They set thresholds on composite indices (the fish Index of Biotic Integrity, the Modified Index of well-being, and the Invertebrate Community Index) rather than on taxa richness, so applying one to a richness count would compare different quantities. Those indices are computed under Ohio EPA's own field protocol against metric lines calibrated on Ohio reference sites, and the NRSA archive carries no index column and cannot derive one. They are Ohio water quality standards keyed to a per-waterbody use designation, while 26 of this ecoregion's 51 stations lie in Indiana. No suitable basis was found among the sources evaluated, which is not a finding that this function cannot be scored. No curve was forced and the function is reported as unassessed, so the ecosystem condition index is stated as an interval.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 16 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a parent ecoregion, stating the level and the transfer risk. 2 carry the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds no stream clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 2 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

The fitted expectation did not pass the recovery test for this metric.

Every published biological criterion in the STAF assessment library is scored on a state-specific field index (Michigan Procedure 51, the Carolina IBI scores, the Wisconsin and Minnesota IBIs), none of which can be computed from NRSA data, so none measures the same quantity as this metric. Ohio EPA's ecoregional biocriteria, the nearest published criterion for this ecoregion, were checked on 2026-09-21 and are not usable either. They set thresholds on composite indices rather than on taxa richness, those indices are computed under Ohio's own field protocol and are not carried by the NRSA archive, and they are Ohio water quality standards while half this ecoregion's stations lie in Indiana.

Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on hydraulic conductivity, precipitation, surficial lithology. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level III, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is high and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 3 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The Level II pool (8.3): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The NARS-9 pool (SAP): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The Level I pool (8): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. No other basis supports it either. National reference: 19 matched national donors, but in the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. 8 national donors inside the comparability envelope, below the floor of 10. Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

metrics.sourceCitation: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy
metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.
metrics.methodContext: Number of dams in the USACE National Inventory of Dams within one mile of the site. DEEP counts them. Note in the field any barrier the inventory does not show.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 30 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 borrows comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

library.author: StreamCurves regional analysis (STAF)
library.revisionNotes: Reference condition is the fixed landscape-pressure screen least-disturbed-v1 (strict), wadeable non-canal frame. 56 of 146 stations of this ecoregion pass. 30 reference curves use local stations, 1 borrow from a wider region, 5 metrics use fixed criteria, and 0 metrics are withheld for insufficient reference support.

metrics.sourceCitation: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy
metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.
metrics.methodContext: Number of dams in the USACE National Inventory of Dams within one mile of the site. DEEP counts them. Note in the field any barrier the inventory does not show.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

exclusions.justification: Every candidate metric for this function (Wetland) was withheld. No station pool from this ecoregion or a wider region under the regional screen passed acceptance, no comparable national reference passed, no approved modeled reference applies here, and the verified catalog holds no applicable published criterion. No curve was forced. The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 18 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 4 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 3 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

metrics.howToMeasure: Mapped dams within one mile is scored on the same fixed criteria EASI uses in every region. Good 0 mapped dams, Fair 1 mapped dam, Poor ≥2 mapped dams.

curve.layerName: EASI fixed criteria, Nearby dam-proximity proxy

curveCaveats: EASI lists the criteria for this metric as provisional, so the breakpoints may be revised.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

metrics.basisStatement: Scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's.
metrics.basisLimit: A published criterion is not an estimate of this ecoregion's reference condition and may disagree with a reference curve where one exists.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 18 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 4 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 3 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 20 of these curves carried forward unchanged from version 1. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.
